source_evidence.observation: The standing problem is a real, nonsingular, general square linear system with A in R^(n x n) and nonzero b in R^n.

source_evidence.anchor: opening paragraphs of Section 2, standard floating-point model and hat notation
source_evidence.observation: The paper invokes the standard floating-point arithmetic model, writes fl(.) for a computed expression, and uses hats for computed quantities.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning 'Our error analysis uses both the 2-norm and the Frobenius norm'
source_evidence.observation: The notation ||.||_2 denotes the 2-norm and ||.||_F denotes the Frobenius norm; for matrices the displayed 2-norm is the induced norm.

source_evidence.anchor: sentence beginning 'The forward error of a computed solution'
source_evidence.observation: For comparison, the paper defines the forward error of x_hat as ||x_hat - x||_2 / ||x||_2.

source_evidence.anchor: unnumbered display beginning 'min { epsilon : (A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b'
source_evidence.observation: The normwise backward error is the minimum common relative bound on simultaneous perturbations of A and b, and the display identifies that minimum exactly with ||b - A x_hat||_2 divided by ||A||_F ||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2.
Thereafter, the unqualified term 'backward error' means this normwise backward error.

binders: Fix the system dimension n, a real matrix A in R^(n x n), and a real vector b in R^n. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'equation (1.1), Ax = b'.]

Let x be the exact solution of Ax = b and let x_hat denote a computed solution; the role of x is inherited from the system and the immediately preceding forward-error definition. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'equation (1.1), Ax = b'; PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'The forward error of a computed solution'.]

Inside the backward-error minimum, epsilon is the common perturbation bound and Delta A and Delta b are perturbations compatible with A and b; their scalar and dimensional types are conventional but not written explicitly in the display. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'min { epsilon : (A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b'.]
hypotheses: A is nonsingular and square. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'a nonsingular general square linear system'.]
The right-hand side satisfies b != 0. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor '0 != b in R^n' in equation (1.1).]

The candidate x_hat is described as a computed solution of (1.1); no residual-size, nonzero, or algorithm-specific condition on x_hat is imposed in the definition. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'the normwise backward error of x_hat we are using is defined as'.]
conclusions: The normwise backward error of x_hat is min { epsilon : (A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b, ||Delta A||_F <= epsilon ||A||_F, ||Delta b||_2 <= epsilon ||b||_2 }. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum'.]

This minimum is exactly ||b - A x_hat||_2 / (||A||_F ||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2). [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'normalized-residual identity' at the right-hand side of the unnumbered display.]
definitions_and_conventions: A hat marks a computed quantity, so x_hat is computed rather than the exact solution x. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'we put a hat on variables to denote that they represent computed quantities'.]
The immediately preceding forward-error definition is ||x_hat - x||_2 / ||x||_2. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'The forward error of a computed solution'.]
In the remainder of the paper, 'backward error' without qualification refers to this normwise backward error. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'In the remainder of this article'.]
implicit_context: Compatibility of the perturbed equation implies Delta A has matrix shape n x n, while x_hat and Delta b have vector dimension n; these types are inherited from equation (1.1), not explicitly bound in the minimum display. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'equation (1.1), Ax = b'; PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '(A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b'.]

The set-builder notation conventionally means that, for each admissible epsilon, perturbations Delta A and Delta b exist simultaneously and satisfy all three displayed conditions. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'min { epsilon : (A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b'.]

Because A is nonsingular and b is nonzero, ||A||_F and ||b||_2 are positive; hence the normalized-residual denominator is positive even when x_hat = 0. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'nonsingular general square linear system' and '0 != b'; PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '||A||_F ||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2'.]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The characterization is stated for a computed solution of the system (1.1) and does not restrict how that solution was produced; in particular, the displayed definition names no GMRES variant, iteration, preconditioner, or orthogonalization method. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'the normwise backward error of x_hat we are using is defined as'.]
numerical_model: The surrounding notation invokes the standard floating-point arithmetic model, uses fl(.) for computed expressions, and uses hats for computed quantities. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'We use the standard model of floating-point arithmetic'.]

The backward-error characterization itself contains no unit roundoff, rounding operation, gamma factor, or precision parameter and is presented as an exact equality. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum and normalized-residual identity'.]
error_notions: The selected notion is a normwise backward error allowing simultaneous perturbation of both the coefficient matrix and the right-hand side. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '(A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b'.]

Both perturbations are measured relatively, against ||A||_F and ||b||_2 respectively, using the same epsilon. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '||Delta A||_F <= epsilon ||A||_F, ||Delta b||_2 <= epsilon ||b||_2'.]
The residual characterization uses the unperturbed residual b - A x_hat. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '||b - A x_hat||_2'.]
norms: Delta A and A are measured in the Frobenius norm. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '||Delta A||_F <= epsilon ||A||_F'.]

Delta b, b, x_hat, and the residual b - A x_hat are measured in the vector 2-norm. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '||Delta b||_2 <= epsilon ||b||_2' and the normalized-residual identity.]

The denominator is the sum ||A||_F ||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2, not a maximum, product of all three norms, or expression using ||A||_2. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'normalized-residual identity'.]
constants_and_indexing: A single common scalar epsilon bounds both relative perturbations; no separate matrix and right-hand-side tolerances appear. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '||Delta A||_F <= epsilon ||A||_F, ||Delta b||_2 <= epsilon ||b||_2'.]

No iteration index, basis-size index, dimension-dependent constant, or index offset occurs in this characterization; n only supplies the system dimensions through (1.1). [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'equation (1.1)'; PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum'.]
higher_order_terms: The minimum and normalized residual are connected by an exact equality; the display contains no big-O term, neglected second-order term, or approximate inequality. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum and normalized-residual identity'.]
exceptional_values: The standing assumptions exclude singular A and b = 0. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'a nonsingular general square linear system' and '0 != b'.]

The definition does not exclude x_hat = 0, and nonzero b keeps its displayed denominator nonzero in that case. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor '0 != b'; PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor '||A||_F ||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2'.]

No NaN, infinity, overflow, underflow, or division-by-zero convention is stated in the selected definition. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum and normalized-residual identity'.]

undebatable_constraints: The standing system is real, square, nonsingular, and has nonzero right-hand side. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'equation (1.1)'.]

The perturbation relation is exactly (A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b, so both A and b may be perturbed simultaneously. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum'.]
The same epsilon bounds ||Delta A||_F / ||A||_F and ||Delta b||_2 / ||b||_2. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'two perturbation inequalities'.]
The exact value is the 2-norm of b - A x_hat divided by ||A||_F ||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'normalized-residual identity'.]
The matrix scaling uses the Frobenius norm, while vectors and the residual use the 2-norm. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'normwise backward-error display'.]

The result is an exact minimum identity without higher-order terms or algorithm-dependent constants. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum and normalized-residual identity'.]

ambiguities.issue: The display does not explicitly bind Delta A, Delta b, or their dimensions.
ambiguities.evidence: Their dimensions are recoverable only from A in R^(n x n), b in R^n, and the equation (A + Delta A)x_hat = b + Delta b. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'equation (1.1)'; PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'perturbed equation in the backward-error display'.]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must supply Delta A in R^(n x n) and Delta b in R^n and must make their existential role explicit; those binders are inherited rather than literally printed.

ambiguities.issue: The scalar domain of epsilon and an explicit condition epsilon >= 0 are omitted.
ambiguities.evidence: The display writes only 'min { epsilon :' followed by norm inequalities. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'beginning of the unnumbered backward-error display'.]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must choose a real or nonnegative-real domain. For the standing nonsingular A, feasibility of the displayed norm inequalities already forces a real epsilon to be nonnegative.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'computed solution' does not specify an algorithm or the detailed axioms of the referenced standard floating-point model.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper gives only the general hat convention and then defines the error for a computed solution of (1.1), with no algorithmic condition in the display. [Evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchors 'standard model of floating-point arithmetic', 'hat on variables', and 'normwise backward error of x_hat'.]
ambiguities.impact: The identity should not be specialized to a particular GMRES implementation or augmented with rounding hypotheses; its mathematical content depends only on A, b, x_hat, the perturbations, and the stated norms.

contract_plain_english: For a real nonsingular square system Ax = b with b nonzero, take any quantity x_hat designated as a computed solution. Its normwise backward error is the smallest common relative tolerance epsilon for which one can perturb A in Frobenius norm and b in 2-norm so that x_hat exactly solves the perturbed system. The paper states the exact closed form ||b - A x_hat||_2 / (||A||_F ||x_hat||_2 + ||b||_2), with no algorithm restriction, rounding term, or asymptotic remainder. [Evidence: PDF p. 1, printed p. 1939, anchor 'equation (1.1)'; PDF p. 4, printed p. 1942, anchor 'unnumbered normwise backward-error minimum and normalized-residual identity'.]
